title: aster novi-belgii subsp. johannensis
intro: Aster novi-belgii subsp. johannensis, commonly known as Johann's Michaelmas daisy, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native to the mountainous regions of Germany and Austria. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, improving digestion, and boosting the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Johann's Michaelmas daisy include anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antiviral properties, which may be attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. Further research is needed to confirm the bioactive constituents and their effects, but preliminary studies suggest that this plant may have antioxidant, anti-cancer, and anti-diabetic properties.
